Known as 'Cyberpunk 2077's' biggest fan, Angharad is a Welsh games writer who thrives in anything related to digital storytelling. If a video game explores the intricacies and horrors of womanhood, she is there.
Thanks to previous work at GAMINGbible, GameByte, The Loadout, Game Luster, Angharad has built a strong understanding of both the digital world and what fans want from it and is eager to share her thoughts and expertise with readers.

Serving as the second remake of the very first Tomb Raider game, Tomb Raider: Legacy Of Atlantis is set to launch on 12 February 2027, after being delayed from its original 2 June 2026 arrival. Courtesy of Crystal Dynamics and Flying Wild Hog, with Amazon Game Studios serving as publisher, Legacy of Atlantis will see the return of Lara Croft as she hunts for a powerful relic from the lost civilization of Atlantis.

With a brand-new Lara Croft at the helm, this time played by Alix Wilton Regan, it will mark a new era for the Tomb Raider franchise, and to celebrate, players can already bag themselves a free outfit which they will be able to unlock once the game launches next year.

Although we have already seen sneak peeks of Lara's new-look in Tomb Raider: Legacy Of Atlantis, including her iconic tank top, shorts, and boots combo, there is no doubt, like the recent Tomb Raider Survivor Trilogy, that we will be able to unlock additional outfits for our explorer throughout the game.

Well, even before the launch of Tomb Raider: Legacy Of Atlantis, we can already style Lara and to do so, all you have to do is create an Amazon Games iD account and sync it with your platform of choice: Steam, PSN, or Xbox.

Once linked, you will unfortunately have to go back to waiting for the launch of Tomb Raider: Legacy Of Atlantis, but when you boot up the game in February, you will have immediate access to The Mediterranean Wetsuit Outfit for Lara. As you can imagine, this is more than your simple wetsuit, serving as more of a wetsuit/swimsuit combination with accompanying tool belt and thigh holsters. There will also be a matching backpack and diving goggles, with Lara herself sporting a high ponytail.

It is an exciting time for Tomb Raider fans, as not only will the new year bring a classic remake, but we can also look forward to Tomb Raider: Catalyst, which currently has a 2028 release window. Also developed by Crystal Dynamics and published by Amazon Game Studios, it will be the fourteenth main entry in the Tomb Raider franchise and will serve as a sequel to 2008's Tomb Raider: Underworld.

We can only imagine that free exclusives will also appear for Tomb Raider: Catalyst closer to its launch, but for now, all the attention is on Tomb Raider: Legacy Of Atlantis, which is set to launch on PC, PlayStation 5, and Xbox Series X/S on 12 February.
